messages:
Eli (Customer Success): Acme reported intermittent 500s & big p95/p99 latency spikes over the last 48h. They've pasted a few timestamps but no request ids. Can we confirm exactly what to ask them to send so we can reproduce and escalate?

Maya (Support): Yes — short checklist to request from customers: 1) one or more request IDs (or the full response body if they have it), 2) a HAR from Chrome/Edge (or a curl capture), 3) SDK logs (if using our SDKs) with debug headers, 4) the exact request payload(s) + model + params, and 5) timezone & approximate local timestamps for each failing call.

Raj (Eng): Quick additions from infra side: include the client timestamp (ISO format) and the region they hit (us-east-1 / eu-west-1 etc.). If they can reproduce, a single curl that reproduces the failure is ideal. Also we like to get the x-redwood-request-id header value from the response — that maps directly to our trace in the backend.

Maya (Support): Practical copy-paste we can send to customer: 

---
Hi — thanks for the report. To help us reproduce and debug this quickly please attach the following: 

1) Request IDs or response snippets: for each failure, please paste the exact server response JSON (including any `request_id` / `x-redwood-request-id` you see). If you don't have the full JSON, just the `request_id` value is fine.

2) HAR from your browser (if this happened from browser):
- In Chrome: Open DevTools -> Network tab -> reproduce the issue -> right-click the network list -> "Save all as HAR with content". Attach the .har file.

3) Curl reproduction (if possible): share the exact curl you used or run the request with verbose headers so we can see response headers (we need to see `x-redwood-request-id`):

```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","input":"<your prompt>","max_tokens":64}'
```
The `-i` prints response headers; look for `x-redwood-request-id` in the response.

4) SDK logs (if using our SDK): enable debug logging and capture the logs around the failing call. For Node: set `DEBUG=redwood*` or add a small snippet to print response headers: 

```
const res = await client.generate(...)
console.log('res status', res.status)
console.log('res headers', res.headers['x-redwood-request-id'])
```

5) Time details: list the customer-visible timestamp(s) (ISO) for each failing call, and the timezone.

6) If you see 401/403/429: include the full response body and the first 8 characters of the API key used (do NOT share full keys). For billing or quota questions, include your account id or org id from the Console.

7) Attach any screenshots, the HAR, and the curl command as files. If the SDK produced a debug bundle, upload that bundle.

---

Maya (Support): Also tell them we can generate a debugging token if they can provide a request id — we can attach internal logs for that id and share a short summary.

Raj (Eng): For internal triage notes: when we receive a request id we search traces by `x-redwood-request-id`. If there's a 500 we look for the exception bytes + backend node id and routing decisions. For latency we check kernel scheduling, batching windows, and whether the request used a cached KV prefix.

support-bot: New ticket created: #SUP-7123 and linked to this thread.

Eli (Customer Success): I'll send that checklist to Acme right now. I'll ask them specifically for one clear repro with a curl + `x-redwood-request-id` and the HAR from Chrome. Can you also confirm we prefer `x-redwood-request-id` over generic `x-request-id` in our docs?

Raj (Eng): Yes — prefer `x-redwood-request-id` (that's what our trace indexing uses). If they only have a generic `request_id` field in the JSON body that's also fine (we map both).

Maya (Support): One more tip: ask them to reproduce once and not to rotate keys while reproducing. Also request the client IP if possible (we can correlate to the infra side).

Eli (Customer Success): Acme replied with 3 request ids: `r-2026-03-12-9a1b2c`, `r-2026-03-13-4d5e6f`, `r-2026-03-14-7g8h9i`. They've attached a HAR and the verbose curl output with response headers. Uploading to the ticket now.

Maya (Support): Great — I'll pull the traces and paste findings back here. :thumbsup:

Raj (Eng): I'll standby for the traces. If any of those show repeated 500s with the same stack, we may need an infra roll or config tweak.

Maya (Support): ETA: I'll respond to customer within 90 minutes after I finish the trace lookup and attach the initial notes.

Eli (Customer Success): Thanks team!
